userStories.title: Paper skeleton, pinned Tectonic build and generated number macros
userStories.description: Create paper/ as in 22.6 with the 22.2 section skeleton, a pinned Tectonic build that fails on log errors, and numbers.py. Its generated/numbers.tex holds no macros until a release bundle with results exists.
acceptanceCriteria: paper/main.tex is a one-column \documentclass[11pt]{article} using paper/arxiv.sty, a style written for this repository with no template code copied. The style sets geometry (letterpaper, 1 in margins) and loads natbib (authoryear, round), amsmath, amssymb, booktabs, xcolor, graphicx and hyperref. It uses Tectonic's default Latin Modern fonts without fontenc or inputenc. The title is the 22.1 working title, with a comment that the final title is set after G5. The author line is the team name Gradient Descent until the listed authors are decided (22.1). \date{} is empty, never \today.

main.tex inputs generated/numbers.tex in the preamble and abstract.tex inside the abstract environment. Then come introduction, background, data, fingerprint, architecture, embedding, training, results, limitations and conclusion, then \appendix, appendix-data-analysis and appendix-embeddings. Each section file holds only \section{<title>} and \label{sec:<file stem>}, with the 22.2 titles: Introduction, Background, Data, Physics fingerprint, Model architecture, Why learn a terrain embedding, Training, Results, Limitations, Conclusion, Data analysis, Embedding visualisations. abstract.tex is empty. No prose, numbers or placeholder text is written. Appendix C is not created, because section 24 has not run.

scripts/numbers.py writes generated/numbers.tex deterministically, with LF line endings and a trailing newline. The first line is '% Generated by paper/scripts/numbers.py. Do not edit; run make -C paper numbers.' A second comment line names the source. Then comes one \newcommand{\<Name>}{<value>} per entry of a MACROS spec, where each entry gives a name of ASCII letters only, a bundle-relative JSON file, a JSON pointer and a format. MACROS is empty in this story, so the committed file holds only the two comment lines, and the source line says that no release bundle was read. This story creates no figures target, no scripts/figures.py and no measurement-review.json, because nothing exists yet to plot or review.

With --bundle <dir>, numbers.py first calls terraluna_pipeline.export.validate_bundle(dir, production=True); the Makefile passes ../release/$(BUNDLE_VERSION) when BUNDLE_VERSION is set. A mock bundle, a null shipping_mode, a missing or unlisted file, or a SHA-256 or byte-count mismatch stops it with exit 1. It prints every error and leaves generated/numbers.tex unchanged. The source line then records bundle_version and the SHA-256 of manifest.json. A macro is an error, never 0 or an empty macro, when its file is not listed in the manifest, its pointer is missing, or its value is null, non-finite or not a number. Duplicate names and names with non-letters are errors.

test_numbers.py is written and run failing before numbers.py exists. It uses temporary bundles written with terraluna_pipeline.export.write_bundle (bundle_version 'test-0', mock false, shipping_mode 'A', never committed). It covers: without a bundle the output is the header-only file, byte-identical over two runs; a one-macro spec renders the expected \newcommand line; a file changed after bundling fails and leaves the output untouched; fixtures/mock-bundle fails; a missing pointer, a null, NaN and a string value each fail; a duplicate name and a name with a digit fail.

test_manuscript.py is written first. Each rule is also tested on short strings that must fail or pass. (1) Section and appendix titles, in include order, equal the 22.2 lists; Exploratory quantum experiment is allowed only as a third appendix. (2) No .tex file under paper/ contains TODO, TBD, FIXME, XX or a longer word of only X, ??, or lorem in any case. (3) In abstract.tex, training.tex, results.tex and appendix-*.tex, no digit appears outside comments and the arguments of \ref, \eqref, \label, \input and the \cite family, so every measurement there is a macro or a generated table. (4) The abstract has at most 200 words after LaTeX is stripped, a macro counting as one word. (5) The \input{figures/...} targets equal PLANNED_FIGURES, which is empty now. Each planned file has exactly one figure environment. No raster image (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, tif, tiff, webp) exists under paper/, and \includegraphics may load only .pdf files under figures/generated/. (6) Every file in generated/ starts with its generated-file comment, and numbers.tex holds only comment and \newcommand lines. Test inputs are strings or files in tmp_path; no fixture .tex file is committed under paper/.

scripts/check_log.py runs after Tectonic on main.log, and on main.blg if it exists. It fails on undefined citations or references, 'Label(s) may have changed', 'Missing character', an Overfull \hbox wider than 1pt, and any BibTeX error or warning. Tectonic 0.17.0 exits 0 even when BibTeX reports errors (observed on this Mac), so this script is what makes them block the build. Unit tests run each pattern on a short log excerpt, and a clean excerpt passes.

paper/Makefile uses POSIX sh recipes and works with GNU Make 3.81. It defines TECTONIC ?= tectonic, UV ?= uv, an empty BUNDLE_VERSION, and TECTONIC_BUNDLE ?= https://relay.fullyjustified.net/default_bundle_v33.tar. That is the default bundle of Tectonic 0.17.0; its cache digest was 6ffe055852f8faf66c0acbe1a7fb27f87b869a90bad1204f3bf4d9683f597c7c when checked on 14 November. The default target, all, runs numbers, test and pdf in that order. If $(TECTONIC) is not on PATH, pdf fails with 'tectonic not found: install it with brew install tectonic (tested with 0.17.0), see paper/README.md'. Otherwise pdf prints the Tectonic version, runs $(TECTONIC) --keep-logs --bundle $(TECTONIC_BUNDLE) main.tex, then runs check_log.py. numbers-check regenerates into a temporary file and exits non-zero with the diff on drift. test runs pytest on scripts/. check runs ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy --strict on scripts/, configured in paper/ruff.toml and paper/mypy.ini. Python runs through $(UV) run --frozen in the existing root workspace. No dependency is added, and pyproject.toml and uv.lock stay unchanged.

main.pdf, main.log and main.blg stay ignored through the existing root .gitignore entries, and no Tectonic output is committed. paper/README.md is short. It lists the prerequisites: make setup at the root, brew install tectonic (tested with 0.17.0), and network access on the first build to fill Tectonic's cache. It names the pinned bundle and states that generated/ is never edited by hand. It lists only the make -C paper commands that ran successfully in this iteration, one line each. The root README, Makefile and .gitignore stay unchanged. A proposed line for the root README goes under 'Proposed instruction changes' in progress.txt.

userStories.title: Prose linter and abstract-overlap check
userStories.description: Make the 22.6 prose rules and the 12-word overlap rule against cited abstracts blocking steps of make -C paper. Both share one LaTeX-to-prose extraction.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared module in scripts/ turns a .tex file into prose that keeps source line numbers. It removes comments (an unescaped % to the end of the line) and inline and display math: $...$, \(...\), \[...\], and the equation, align, gather and multline environments with their starred forms. It removes verbatim and \verb, and the arguments of the \cite family, \ref, \eqref, \label, \input, \include and \url, plus the URL argument of \href. It also removes the code of tikzpicture environments. It keeps the text arguments of formatting commands such as \emph, \textit and \textbf, and reads ~ as a space. lint_prose.py and overlap_check.py both use this module.

lint_prose.py checks every .tex file under paper/ except figures/styles.tex, which is style code. It prints 'file:line: rule: text' for each finding and exits 1 if there is any finding. No option disables a rule.

The rules. (a) Dash punctuation: U+2012 to U+2015 and the other Unicode dashes, \textemdash, \textendash, and --- anywhere. Also -- or an en dash, except directly between two digits as a numeric range (9--11), and a hyphen with whitespace on both sides. Hyphens inside words and minus signs in math are allowed. (b) Banned words, matched case-insensitively as whole words with their inflections (delves, leveraged, showcasing, underscores, empowering): delve, seamless, robust, leverage, cutting-edge, comprehensive, crucial, pivotal, showcase, innovative, harness, groundbreaking, game-changing, tapestry, testament, underscore, unlock, empower. Only robust can be allowed, and only on a line that carries the comment '% lint-allow robust: <reason>' with a non-empty reason. (c) The phrase 'it is important to note', in any case, also across line breaks and markup. (d) Any ? in prose, which catches rhetorical questions. (e) Bullet lists: itemize, enumerate or description environments in main.tex, abstract.tex and the ten main-body section files. They are allowed in appendix-*.tex. (f) Bold inside sentences: \textbf, \bfseries or {\bf ...} outside tabular environments. Rules b and c also run on the raw text of tikzpicture environments. The other rules skip TikZ code, where -- and -> are path syntax.

overlap_check.py tokenises the prose of the files that lint_prose.py checks, and every non-null abstract in paper/reference-verification.json, read from references.<key>.abstract. Tokenising applies Unicode NFKC, folds LaTeX accent commands and diacritics to base letters, case-folds, and splits the text into runs of [a-z0-9]. Hyphens, punctuation, ties and line breaks therefore cannot make the two sides tokenise differently. Any run of 12 or more consecutive tokens shared with a single abstract fails. Each maximal run is reported once, with file, line, reference key and the shared words. The limit of 12 is a constant, and no option raises it. A missing or unparsable record file fails. Entries whose abstract is null are skipped and counted in the summary line.
paper/reference-verification.json is created as {"references": {}}. T16-03 defines the rest of the record, and the citation-checker stories fill it.

test_lint_prose.py and test_overlap_check.py are written and run failing before the scripts exist. Lint cases: 'a --- b' and an em dash fail, while 'pages 9--11', '$a-b$', 'self-supervised' and a dash inside a % comment pass. 'Leveraging' and '\emph{seamless}' fail. 'robust' fails alone and passes with the allow comment, while 'leverage' still fails with an allow comment. 'it is' followed by a line break and 'important to note' fails. 'Why?' fails and '\url{https://x.org/?q=1}' passes. itemize fails in background.tex and passes in appendix-data-analysis.tex. '\textbf{x}' fails in prose and passes inside tabular. '\draw (a) -- (b);' inside tikzpicture passes. Overlap cases: 12 shared words fail and 11 pass. A change of case, a line break, \emph{...}, a ~ tie or an inserted %-comment line does not hide a 12-word run. 'self-supervised' matches 'self supervised', and \'e matches e with an acute accent. Six words from one abstract followed by six from another pass. A missing record file fails. Test inputs are strings or files in tmp_path; no fixture .tex file is committed under paper/.

The lint and overlap targets run the two scripts, and all now runs numbers, lint, overlap, test and pdf in that order. The current manuscript passes both checks. paper/README.md gains one line for each new command that ran.
userStories.notes: ralph orchestrator 2026-11-14T21:42:04Z: T16-02 reached the 4-round limit with 4 fixed blocker findings in round 4, all adversarial LaTeX edge cases. Decision: this loop runs with up to 6 review rounds (RALPH_MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS=6). Scope clarification for the author and the reviewers: lint_prose.py and overlap_check.py enforce PRD 22.6 and D36 on prose that authors actually write; they are not a security boundary against deliberately crafted LaTeX. Fix every finding that a realistic manuscript could trigger. A finding that needs contrived input no author would write (for example escaped environment spellings built to fake an exemption) may be rebutted with this reason, citing PRD 22.6. No rule, banned word, threshold or test is weakened.

userStories.title: Reference record contract, generated refs.bib and citation tests
userStories.description: Define and validate paper/reference-verification.json, and generate refs.bib from it for cited keys only. An uncited, unverified or hand-edited bibliography entry then fails the build.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/references.py defines the record with pydantic v2 models, which are already in the workspace environment. Extra fields are forbidden and every field is required; optional values are typed X | None and must still be present. The top level is {method, references}. Each reference key maps to: status (verified or unresolved), unresolvedReason, entryType (article, inproceedings, misc, techreport, phdthesis, book or incollection), and fields, which map BibTeX field names to values. Field names come from a fixed set: author, title, journal, booktitle, year, volume, number, pages, publisher, doi, eprint, archiveprefix, primaryclass, url, howpublished, institution, school, note, month, editor. The remaining keys are primaryUrl, sourceKind (publisher, arxiv, ads or provider), metadataUrl, searchQuery, checked (an ISO date), verifiedFields, evidence, abstract, abstractSource, abstractUnavailableReason, and supports, a list of {claim, location}.

Validation rules. (1) Keys match ^[a-z]+[0-9]{4}[a-z]*$: the first author's surname, the year and an optional disambiguator, such as tolometti2022holuhraun. (2) A verified record has author, title and year. Its verifiedFields equal the set of its fields keys. It has at least one supports entry with a non-empty claim and a location (page, section, figure, table or abstract), and its unresolvedReason is null. An unresolved record has a non-empty unresolvedReason. (3) A doi matches ^10\.\d{4,9}/\S+$; the primaryUrl is then https://doi.org/<doi> and the sourceKind is publisher. Without a doi, an eprint is a new-style arXiv id without version (^\d{4}\.\d{4,5}$) with archiveprefix arXiv, primaryUrl https://arxiv.org/abs/<eprint> and sourceKind arxiv. An ads source needs a https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/ URL. provider is only for data products and official documentation. (4) A verified publisher, arxiv or ads record has a non-empty verbatim abstract and an https abstractSource; a provider record may have a null abstract only with an abstractUnavailableReason. (5) primaryUrl, metadataUrl and abstractSource may not point to these secondary hosts: typeset.io, unpaywall.org, doaj.org, researchgate.net, semanticscholar.org, scholar.google.com, wikipedia.org, academia.edu, eos.org, experts.arizona.edu, jrskok.com. These are aggregators, profiles, news summaries and personal copies, several of which PRD 25 links. metadataUrl and abstractSource may be the publisher-deposited Crossref record https://api.crossref.org/works/<doi>. (6) A field value with unbalanced braces fails.

'references.py check' validates the record and prints every error with its key and field. 'references.py bib' writes refs.bib for exactly the keys cited in the manuscript: \cite, \citet, \citep, \citealt, \citealp, \citeauthor, \citeyear and their starred forms, with comma-separated keys. Entries are sorted by key, with fields in a fixed order, values in braces, a 2-space indent, LF line endings and one blank line between entries. The file starts with a comment saying that it is generated and must not be edited, and ends with a trailing newline. A cited key that is missing or unresolved is an error that names the key and its source line. The output is byte-identical across runs.

test_manuscript.py gains these checks: every cited key has a verified record; the refs.bib keys equal the cited keys; refs.bib equals the generator output; and main.tex contains \bibliographystyle{plainnat} and \bibliography{refs} exactly when the manuscript cites at least one key. The last rule exists because BibTeX reports an error on a bibliography with no citations (observed with Tectonic 0.17.0).

test_references.py is written and run failing before references.py exists. A valid verified record passes. Each rule fails on a minimal counter-example: a bad key, an arxiv record without an abstract, verifiedFields missing one field, a DOI with an arXiv primaryUrl, an eprint with a version suffix, a doi.org URL that differs from the doi field, a typeset.io primaryUrl, an unknown field, an unresolved record without a reason, and unbalanced braces. Citing an unresolved key fails generation. A record that is not cited stays out of refs.bib. Two generator runs give identical bytes.

The bib target regenerates refs.bib. refs-check validates the record, regenerates refs.bib into a temporary file and fails with a diff on drift. all now runs numbers, bib, references.py check, lint, overlap, test and pdf in that order. paper/README.md gains one line for each new command that ran.

After this story the record holds no references: references is {}, and method states how references are verified (the primary page read, the fields compared, the abstract source). refs.bib holds only its generated comment, and main.tex has no \bibliography, because nothing is cited yet.

userStories.title: Verify the roughness and radar-polarimetry references
userStories.description: Verify at primary sources the works that Background 2.1 and 2.2 will cite, and record them with their abstracts and the claims they support.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of these works has a record that is either verified or unresolved with a concrete reason, for example that no allowed source shows the abstract. (1) Shepard et al. 2001, the roughness of natural terrain (E3). (2) Rosenburg et al. 2011, global surface slopes and roughness of the Moon from LOLA: the JGR Planets article, not the 2014 thesis chapter that E4 links. (3) Kreslavsky et al. 2013, lunar topographic roughness maps from LOLA (E5). (4) Kreslavsky and Head 2000, kilometre-scale roughness of Mars from MOLA (22.2). (5) Campbell and Shepard 1996 (R02). (6) Campbell 2012, high circular polarization ratios (R07). (7) Raney et al. 2011, the Mini-RF hybrid polarimetric architecture (C4). (8) The Raney et al. paper that defines the m-chi decomposition for hybrid polarimetry; C3 links an IGARSS 2012 DOI, so the record names the publication the definition is taken from. (9) Carter et al. 2012, Mini-RF impact melts (B6, C6). (10) Fa and Cai 2013, the CPR of lunar craters (B5). (11) Gao et al. 2023, Mini-RF CPR and rock abundance (B4). (12) Fassett et al. 2024, Mini-RF orthorectification and topographic correction (A3). (13) Rivera-Valentín et al. 2026, S-band polarimetry and surface rocks (R01, C1).

Bibliographic fields, the DOI or arXiv id, and the abstract are read at the publisher (through https://doi.org/<doi>), at arXiv, at NASA ADS or in the publisher-deposited Crossref record. They are never taken from the secondary pages that PRD 25 links for several of these works. No DOI is typed from memory: each one is read at a source and resolves through doi.org. abstract holds the verbatim published abstract, and abstractSource gives the page it was read from.
evidence names the page that was read and the fields compared with it. searchQuery records the query used, and checked is the date of the check.

Each verified record has supports entries, written in the checker's own words with a location in the source, for the claims Background will make. They include the PRD 17 and section 3 claims, each checked at the source: roughness scaling holds only over finite ranges (Campbell and Shepard 1996); valid CPR can exceed unity (Campbell 2012); incidence angle shifts CPR, and high CPR in anomalous polar craters is mostly due to rocks (Fa and Cai 2013); CPR is not monotonic with rock abundance, and several polarimetric properties together resolve the ambiguity (Rivera-Valentín et al. 2026); the Fassett et al. 2024 δCPR and δS1 layers are empirically normalised quantities, not CPR values (D13). A claim that the source does not support is not recorded, and the PRD's wording is not evidence. A number in a supports claim is copied exactly, with its location.
Nothing else under paper/ changes. refs.bib stays as generated, because no section cites these keys yet.

userStories.title: Verify the analog-study and learned-representation references
userStories.description: Verify at primary sources the works that Background 2.3 to 2.5 will cite, and record them with their abstracts and the claims they support.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of these works has a record that is either verified or unresolved with a concrete reason. (1) Neish et al. 2017, terrestrial analogues for lunar impact melt flows: the Icarus article, because R06 links a personal copy. (2) Tolometti et al. 2020, lava flow properties at Craters of the Moon from L-band radar (B1). (3) Tolometti et al. 2022, Holuhraun lava types from radar and lidar (B2, C2). (4) The 2020 PSJ study of the surface texture of Martian lava flows (B3). (5) The Qaidam Basin Mars-analog selection study (arXiv 2501.08584, D21). (6) Bardes et al. 2022, VICReg (D23). (7) Ganin et al. 2016, domain-adversarial training (D24). (8) Caron et al. 2021, DINO, the self-supervised ViT behind the DINO baseline of 22.2 section 6. (9) LunarFM (arXiv 2607.22408, D18). PRD 17 says FDL 2025 and D18 says 2026, so the record gives the year that the primary source states. (10) The NASA-IBM lunar foundation model (arXiv 2609.13283, B13). (11) SomBench (arXiv 2609.13277, B13). (12) topo2vec (arXiv 2108.08870, D19). (13) GEAR (arXiv 2603.18626, D20). (14) CraterBench-R (arXiv 2604.06245, D22). (15) Shukla et al. 2024, Mini-RF dielectric constant by deep learning (B8). (16) Aussel et al. 2025, the global lunar boulder map: the primary publication, not the Eos summary that B14 links.

The source and identifier rules of T16-04 apply. Metadata and the verbatim abstract are read at the publisher, arXiv, NASA ADS or the publisher-deposited Crossref record. No identifier is typed from memory. evidence, searchQuery and checked are filled as in T16-04.

supports entries state, in the checker's own words with locations, the claims that PRD 17 attributes to these works, but only where the source itself states them. Neish et al.: lunar impact melts are radar-rough at decimetres yet smooth at metres, and none of the Earth lavas studied matched. Tolometti et al. 2020: L-band CPR separates smoother and rougher flows. Tolometti et al. 2022: the facies are separable by UAVSAR CPR, yet their distributions overlap. LunarFM: parameter count, Moon-only training, latitude limit, chip size and contiguous spatial-holdout behaviour. topo2vec: fractal self-supervision on Earth DEMs. GEAR: expert-labelled Earth-to-Earth analog retrieval. The Qaidam study: a Siamese network pairing Mars and Earth imagery. CraterBench-R: supervised metric-learning fine-tuning can hurt retrieval. Shukla et al.: look direction alone shifts the inversion. Aussel et al.: boulder count, size limit and latitude range. A value the source does not state, such as the PRD's 88 to 89 percent overlap or about 110 million parameters, is recorded only if the source gives it, copied exactly with its location.
Nothing else under paper/ changes. refs.bib stays as generated.

userStories.title: Background section from verified references
userStories.description: Write section 2, Background, from the verified records only. It covers prior work and contains no Terraluna method, data, results or data-dependent claims.
acceptanceCriteria: background.tex keeps \section{Background}\label{sec:background} and has five subsections, in this order. (1) Planetary roughness statistics: the RMS deviation, deviogram and Hurst exponent as Shepard et al. 2001 define them, baselines and breakover after Rosenburg et al. 2011, Kreslavsky et al. 2013, Kreslavsky and Head 2000 for Mars, and finite scaling ranges. (2) Radar polarimetry and the circular polarization ratio. (3) Quantitative analog-site studies. (4) Self-supervised and domain-adversarial learning. (5) Learned planetary and terrain representations, including LunarFM, topo2vec and GEAR. The section uses paragraphs only, with no lists, tables, figures or displayed equations; equations belong to section 4.

The section has 900 to 1,400 words of prose, counted with the same LaTeX stripping as the abstract word count. It uses \citet when the authors are the subject and \citep otherwise, and never types an author-year citation by hand.

Every cited key has a verified record, and each citation sits on a claim that one of that record's supports entries states. Unresolved keys are not cited. The section cites at least the verified records for Shepard et al. 2001, Rosenburg et al. 2011, Kreslavsky et al. 2013, Kreslavsky and Head 2000, VICReg, Ganin et al. 2016, LunarFM, topo2vec and GEAR. If one of these is unresolved, the section leaves it out and progress.txt says so.

Background describes prior work only. It does not describe Terraluna's method, data, configuration values or results. It makes no claim of novelty or of absent prior work ('first', 'novel', 'only', 'no prior work', 'none has'), and it leaves positioning to the Introduction and section 6. Any number it states is a literature value, in a sentence that cites its source, and matches a supports entry. A test added first to test_manuscript.py makes a background.tex sentence fail if it has a digit outside command arguments and no \cite-family command.

The section follows the section 3 wording rules. CPR is sensitive to structure near the wavelength, is not monotonic with rock abundance, and is never presented as a measure of a block size or scale. No continuous measured roughness spectrum is implied. Fassett et al. δCPR and δS1 are normalised context layers, not CPR values (D13). Overlapping distributions are expected. Earth surfaces are candidates for interpreting a signature, never confirmed analogs.

main.tex gains \bibliographystyle{plainnat} and \bibliography{refs} after the conclusion and before \appendix. refs.bib is regenerated with make -C paper bib and holds exactly the cited keys. The PDF builds with every citation resolved and no BibTeX error or warning reported by check_log.py.

The text is written in the author's own words from the records and primary sources, not paraphrased sentence by sentence from abstracts, and lint and overlap pass on it. No other section, the record, or any script other than test_manuscript.py changes.

userStories.title: Shared TikZ styles and the system-overview diagram
userStories.description: Add the shared TikZ styles and one vector diagram of the 8.1 system overview, the only figure allowed before results exist. This story is the first to cut.
acceptanceCriteria: figures/styles.tex is input once from the main.tex preamble. It loads tikz with only the libraries the figure uses and defines the 22.5 styles: flat pastel fills with thin dark outlines, one fill per workload (offline Python, release bundle, hosting, browser), a dashed variant and arrow styles. The fills differ in lightness as well as hue, so they stay distinct in grayscale. There are no icons, gradients, shadows, 3D effects, emoji or included images.

figures/system-overview.tex holds one figure environment with one tikzpicture. It shows exactly the components and arrows of the PRD 8.1 diagram, named as there. terraluna_pipeline and terraluna_ml (offline Python) feed the versioned, checksummed release bundle. The bundle goes to object storage and CDN, and to the Hugging Face Hub mirror. Next.js 16 on Vercel (pages, Hono /api/v1, /api/docs) reads the bundle. The visitor's browser has deck.gl maps, React Three Fiber twins and a Web Worker running @terraluna/core and ONNX Runtime Web. The live probe makes Copernicus GLO-30 COG range reads, directly or through /api/v1/dem.
